mood: Cool, conversational tech insider; measured pace with subtle, dry humor.
transcript: One man in a leather jacket runs AI hardware. His name is Jensen Huang, and he has run Nvidia since he co-founded it in nineteen ninety-three. Nvidia designs the chips that a lot of the biggest AI models are trained on. So when people wonder if he might step down, the whole tech economy leans in. Some people even put real money on it, trading bets on prediction markets like Polymarket. But here is the twist... [short pause] Nvidia does not manufacture its own chips. It designs them. A company called TSMC, in Taiwan, builds them. And the real moat is software. CUDA, a toolkit developers have used for years, is built for Nvidia hardware. Switching chips can mean rewriting a lot of code. Honestly, most companies would rather not. So if he left, the chips would keep shipping and the code would keep running. The revolution would be fine. [short pause] [deadpan] The jacket, though, has no clear successor.
